text: The extract for this entry records the survival of insular Celtic literature. After Ireland, Wales held the richest trove of mythological tales. The White Book of Rhydderech was set down early in the fourteenth century. The Red Book of Hergest followed it about fifty years later. The tales of these two books together form the Mabinogion. This cycle of myths is as rich and complex as any in the literate world. Scotland too had its scribes: the Dean of Lismore compiled a Gaelic manuscript in 1516.

okr.objective: The survival of insular Celtic literature after Ireland.
key_results: Wales held the richest mythological material after Ireland.
The White Book of Rhydderech dates from the early fourteenth century.
The two Welsh books together form the Mabinogion.
The Book of the Dean of Lismore of 1516 records Scots Gaelic works.
